case_studies.title: Detecting Knowledge Inconsistencies Across Text, Tables, and Knowledge Graphs
case_studies.abstract: Wikipedia and Wikidata are widely used for information access, LLM pre-training, and retrieval-augmented generation. Their knowledge is deeply connected but scattered across text, tables, and knowledge graphs. This raises a practical question: when these modalities disagree, how can we detect and explain the conflict? We study this problem as \emph{modality-level inconsistency detection}. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of detecting inconsistencies in knowledge across different formats, such as text, tables, and knowledge graphs, by building a system called Kontras, which can identify and explain conflicts between these formats. The result is a more reliable and trustworthy source of information. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: RepoReasoner: Evaluating Repository-Level Code Reasoning Ability of Long-Context Language Models
case_studies.abstract: Recent large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance on software engineering tasks, yet most existing benchmarks evaluate code reasoning at the function level, where all relevant information is localized. This setting fails to reflect real-world development, which requires reasoning across multiple files and complex dependency structures. We introduce RepoReasoner, a benchmark for evaluating repository-level code reasoning. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating code reasoning at the repository level, beyond just function-level reasoning. The authors built RepoReasoner, a benchmark to assess repository-level code reasoning abilities of long-context language models. The result is a new way to evaluate language models' ability to reason across multiple files and complex dependency structures.

Check if your current models are being used for tasks that require reasoning across multiple files. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of transferring knowledge across different graph domains and tasks without requiring labeled data for each new domain. The result is a model that can be applied to new graph domains without needing additional training data.

case_studies.abstract: Agent skills package reusable procedures that improve downstream performance. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of inferring proprietary skills used by agents from their execution trajectories, the authors built a method to reconstruct these skills, and the result shows that it's possible to expose hidden skills. This affects cloud-hosted agent interfaces where providers try to keep high-value skills proprietary. The research reveals a potential security risk in agent skills packages.

case_studies.title: RSIBench-Data: Benchmarking Data-Centric Research for Recursive Self-Improvement
case_studies.abstract: Recursive self-improvement requires turning evidence of model failures into better models. Data-centric post-training research entails diagnosing capability gaps, designing and validating training-data strategies, and learning from checkpoint feedback. Can LLM agents automate this loop? Existing benchmarks entangle research decisions with optimization, serving, evaluation, and systems implementation, obscuring agents' research capability. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of automating data-centric research for recursive self-improvement in large language models. The researchers built a benchmark called RSIBench-Data to test the ability of LLM agents to automate this process. The result is a controlled benchmark that evaluates the research capability of LLM agents.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage large language models, here is what to do: review your current post-training stack, consider using RSIBench-Data to evaluate your LLM agents' research capability, and explore opportunities to automate data-centric research. This may help improve the performance of your models. Not directly applicable to general cloud infrastructure work, but relevant to those working with LLMs.

case_studies.title: \textsc{IH-Benchmark}: A Conflict-Centered Benchmark for Instruction-Hierarchy Robustness in LLM Applications
case_studies.abstract: When a language model receives conflicting instructions from different priority levels, which one does it actually follow? This question lies at the heart of reliable LLM deployment. Existing benchmarks answer this only partially, often focusing on a single hierarchy edge or adapting public datasets with limited tool-use coverage. We present IH-Benchmark, a conflict-centered benchmark for instruction-hierarchy robustness across direct system-user conflicts (S>U) and tool-mediated user-tool (U>T) conflicts. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of language models receiving conflicting instructions by creating a benchmark called IH-Benchmark to test instruction-hierarchy robustness. The authors built a comprehensive benchmark that covers various conflict scenarios. The result is a tool that helps evaluate the reliability of language models in real-world applications.

case_studies.summary: This research aims to solve the problem of scaling security controls for AI coding agents across organizations, by building a custom agent harness to distribute off-the-shelf security controls. The result is a phased testing methodology that can be applied to commercial AI coding agents. This can help overcome security and risk concerns that hinder the adoption of AI coding agents.
